_note: Every number below was read from the cited source by the author of this file (tables/figures quoted verbatim); nothing is recalled from memory unless a ref says 'unverified'. Isotherm form: q_i = sum_sites qs*K*C_i/(1+sum_j K_j*C_j), K = b0*exp(-dU/(R*T)), C in mol/m3 (concentration basis, as published). presets/sorbent__*.json hold the same numbers converted to the ParamDef basis (b_ref in 1/bar at 298.15 K, Q = -dU + R*298.15 in kJ/mol); regenerate with `python -m vessels.sorbent.build_presets`.

WIL17.cite: N. S. Wilkins, 'Characterizing Adsorbents for Pre- and Post-Combustion Carbon Capture', MSc thesis, Univ. of Alberta (2017); Zeochem 13X Z10-02 / Z10-02ND; Tables 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, Fig. 4.11
WIL17.related: Wilkins & Rajendran, Adsorption 25, 115-133 (2019), doi:10.1007/s10450-018-00004-2 (CO2/N2 part; paywalled, numbers NOT cross-read there). Water fit on 13X after Krishnamurthy et al. (AIChE J. 2014), fitted to Wang & LeVan data (as stated in WIL17 Sec. 4.2.1).

NGU21.cite: T. T. T. Nguyen, 'Humid Post-Combustion CO2 Capture By Vacuum Swing Adsorption Using CALF-20', PhD thesis, Univ. of Alberta (2021); Tables 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 3.1, 4.3, 4.4, A2.1, A4.2, A4.5; Fig. 2.6
NGU21.related: Nguyen et al., Competitive CO2/H2O Adsorption on CALF-20, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 63, 3265 (2024); preprint doi:10.26434/chemrxiv-2023-f3rzv (paywalled; numbers read from the thesis only).

RUTH84.cite: D. M. Ruthven, Principles of Adsorption and Adsorption Processes, Wiley (1984): axial dispersion D_L = 0.7 Dm + v*r_p and LDF resistances in series; read as used in NGU21 eq. 2.5-2.6 and WIL17 eq. 3.4-3.5

WF78.cite: N. Wakao & S. Funazkri, Chem. Eng. Sci. 33, 1375 (1978): Sh = 2 + 1.1 Sc^(1/3) Re^0.6

AE96.cite: Alduchov & Eskridge, J. Appl. Meteorol. 35, 601 (1996), Magnus form p_sat = 610.94*exp(17.625*T/(T+243.04)) Pa, T in C (unverified: recalled, checked against 2.645 kPa at 22 C)

FUL66.cite: Fuller, Schettler & Giddings, Ind. Eng. Chem. 58(5), 18 (1966); He 2.88, H2O 12.7 diffusion volumes (unverified, recalled)

BSL.cite: Bird, Stewart & Lightfoot, Transport Phenomena: Lennard-Jones He sigma 2.551 A, eps/k 10.22 K; H2O 2.641 A, 809.1 K (unverified, recalled)

ROY19.cite: S. Roy & A. S. Moharir, 'Modeling the Generic Breakthrough Curve for Adsorption Process', arXiv:1907.00195, Table 1 (single LDF-Langmuir column)

13X_Z1002ND.label: Zeochem 13X premium Z10-02ND (CO2, N2, H2O)
13X_Z1002ND.ref: WIL17 Table 4.1 (CO2, N2: volumetry 0-100 C to 1.2 bar and gravimetry 25-150 C to 5 bar; H2O: dynamic-column loadings 22-100 C, p_H2O <= 0.025 bar)
13X_Z1002ND.fit_note: CO2/H2O competition was measured only in ~1 bar CO2 (WIL17 Table 4.5); WIL17 reports the extended-DSL over-predicts CO2 there (CO2 breakthrough 'not predicted well'). Treat CO2 loading with RH>0 as an upper bound.
13X_Z1002ND.bed_ref: WIL17 Table 4.4 (22.03 g in 6.4 cm x 2.82 cm column -> 551 kg/m3; cp_s 'assumed'; eps 0.4 measured; eps_p 0.35; tau 3 assumed); particle size of Z10-02ND NOT stated in WIL17 and not found elsewhere: particle_dp_mm keeps its generic default

13X_Z1002.label: Zeochem 13X standard Z10-02 (CO2, N2, H2O)
13X_Z1002.ref: WIL17 Table 4.1 (CO2, N2 volumetry 25-100 C to 1.2 bar; H2O as premium, saturation x1.11 per WIL17 Sec. 4.2.1)
13X_Z1002.fit_note: as 13X_Z1002ND; CO2/N2 data only to 1.2 bar and 100 C

CALF20.label: CALF-20 (1 mm x 1-3 mm extrudate, polysulfone binder)
CALF20.ref: NGU21: CO2 DSL Table 2.1, N2 equal-energy-site scheme Table 2.3 (volumetry 25-100 C, 0-1.2 bar); H2O quadratic-Langmuir (cubic in C) Table 3.1 adsorption branch (22-100 C, p_H2O <= 0.027 bar; desorption branch/hysteresis NOT used); CO2 humidity factors Table 4.3 / A4.2

H2O.form: site1 = qs*(b1*C+2*b2*C^2+3*b3*C^3)/(1+b1*C+b2*C^2+b3*C^3), b_k = b0_k*exp(-dU1/RT); site2 = Langmuir with dU2 (NGU21 eq. 3.13-3.16)

CALF20.alpha_note: NGU21 eq. 4.19-4.21 fitted these at 22 C, 0.97 bar total in a CO2 carrier using the *competitive* water isotherm (Table 4.4 column 2: qsb 1.795, b0 -5.937e-15 / 1.013e-15 / 6.197e-15, dU1 -81.67, qsd 8.056, d0 5.448e-11, dU2 -54.41), which is a 22 C / ~1 bar CO2 effective isotherm and is NOT wired in here. The model uses the pure-water isotherm inside the same factor, so CO2 suppression is over-predicted for dilute CO2 and for T != 22 C.
CALF20.fit_note: competitive CO2/H2O data only at 22 C in ~1 bar CO2 (NGU21 Table 4.2, RH 13-87%)
CALF20.bed_ref: NGU21 Table 2.2 (16.7 g in 7.86 cm x 2.82 cm -> 340 kg/m3; cp_s 1371 'fitted'; eps 0.4 measured; eps_p 0.35, tau 3 assumed; 1.0 mm diameter cylinders p. 27)

benchmarks._note: Experimental comparison data. Loadings are tabulated in the thesis (mass-balance of breakthrough runs, 0.97 bar). Breakthrough times were read off the plotted markers by pixel analysis (+/- 3-5 %), t_bar = t*v/L.

CALF20_loading_CO2_He.cols: y_CO2 (balance He), q_CO2 mol/kg, T C

CALF20_breakthrough_CO2_He.cols: y_CO2 in He, t_bar at 50 % of the plateau (exp. markers; thesis text gives exit at ~50, 62, 87)

13X_Z1002ND_loading_CO2.cols: p_CO2 bar, q_CO2 mol/kg, T C (He carrier, 1 atm)

13X_Z1002ND_competitive.ref: WIL17 Table 4.5 (CO2 + humid CO2, air sweep)

13X_Z1002ND_breakthrough_CO2_He.cols: y_CO2 in He, t_bar at 50 % of plateau (exp+sim lines overlap at the front, +/- 25)

r_macropore_nm (Knudsen correction): no sourced value, off by default
13X particle diameter (Z10-02/ND): not published in WIL17
regen.* (T_regen_K, P_regen_kPa, flow, time): operating choices, not data
no sourced 13X or CALF-20 CO2/H2O competition valid at flue-gas CO2 fractions (data are ~1 bar CO2)
